notes: The South of Market Area Historic Resource Survey (the Eastern Neighborhoods SoMa Area Plan and Western SoMa Community Plan survey, 2007–2010, Page & Turnbull for SF Planning; findings adopted by the HPC 16 February 2011, Resolution No. 103) — the per-property record the 2009 South of Market Area Historic Context Statement cites as 'attached' and does not contain. Read here from its published results table, 'List of Surveyed Properties, sorted by Street Address' (122 PDF pages), with the department's Key (integrity 0–7, architecture 1–5) and the California Historical Resource Status Codes sheet it links. Each row gives the assessor's parcel, a street-number range, the year built as surveyed, a status code, the eligible district where any, the two ratings and a building-notes column that is mostly a historic building or firm name.

coverage.remaining: Nothing of the table. The six district records on the same page are the next batch: South Park (47 pp.), South End Historic District Addition, Bluxome and Townsend, 6th Street Lodginghouse (2 pp.) and the Western SoMa Light Industrial and Residential district (124 pp.), whose narratives describe contributors one by one — the table carries each one's status code and district, not its description. The individual DPR 523A/B forms are reachable only through the survey's interactive map, not fetched.
coverage.note: All 122 pages read, reconstructed from pdftotext -bbox word coordinates (the notes and district columns are bottom-aligned to the row line and wrap upward). 2,140 rows: 644 are buildings under fifty years old or vacant lots with the boilerplate 6Z note and no ratings, not findings; 3 rows lost to the layout (one row printed twice on top of another at 114 Welsh, and 531 Bryant/15 Zoe with no code); 1,493 findings, every one printing its own assessor block and lot.
